text:
anya: quick heads-up — brought up reranker-3b-v2 quantized -> int8. offline results look odd: almost no MRR delta on webquery, but NDCG@10 drops ~2.6% on SERP-core holdout.

sam: huh. is SERP-core the short-title-heavy slice?

anya: yes median query ~6 tokens. eval used same prod preproc (truncate body to 512, strip html), but our eval harness concatenates title+snippet while prod does snippet+title. wondering if formatting/order changes tokenization near boundary.

linh: order changes could shift tokenizer boundaries and KV cache alignment. also check whether score normalization differs between fp16 and int8 kernels.

anya: did a quick swap: changing harness to snippet+title recovers ~1.8% of NDCG gap. so formatting explains most but not all (~0.8% remains).

devon: can you paste exact eval command + seed? I'll try to repro locally with both fp16 and int8.

anya: ```
./eval_rerank.py --model reranker-3b-v2-int8 --holdout datasets/serp-core/holdout.jsonl --preproc config/serp-prod.yaml --batch 64 --seed 42
```

eval-bot: run finished: id=1799994339 | NDCG@10 fp16:0.812 -> int8:0.789 | MRR fp16:0.321 -> int8:0.319

sam: a few hypotheses: tokenizer boundary shift, kvpack alignment differences, or quant rounding interacting with softmax tails. can we dump logits for same inputs and compare?

anya: starting a logits-diff pass now (fp16 vs int8) and will compute per-query delta histogram. pushing logs to /tmp/serp-int8-diff.tar.gz and will link.

linh: also run candidate-order ablation: randomize candidate list order in eval to see sensitivity. formatting should not change order, but priming/position effects can amplify small score shifts into top1 changes.

devon: if formatting is the main driver we can add a lightweight formatting shim in preproc to normalize concat order for canary. smaller change than retraining.

anya: uploaded per-query delta plot (see thread file). short-title cohort concentrated in the left tail. attaching quick sample of 10 queries where int8 flips top1.

sam: nice. once we have the logits diffs and per-query lists, let's pick a golden subset (~200 queries) to run on Dedicated canary with traffic mirror. plan: if NDCG drop <0.5% on gold set, we can stage rollout.

anya: agreed. will post results + logs in this thread when ready. thanks all. :thumbsup:
